title: Choose the visual world for LayerLift
question: The roll assigned Slicer Preview. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Slicer Preview
options.lineage: OrcaSlicer / Bambu Studio preview mode: plate, layer slider, colour legend
options.thesis: LayerLift speaks the slicer's own preview language, so the model on the plate leads and every control reads like a print setting.
options.viewport: Graphite build plate fills the centre with the model on it; a vertical layer scrubber on its right edge; a dense settings column on the left like a process panel; a legend strip (slot, colour, height, grams) under the plate; Export as the one orange action.
options.risk: Can read as an Orca clone if the chrome copies Orca instead of borrowing its grammar.

raised.raise: One rhythm: spacing and row heights step in layer units, so sections read as stacked layers, not floating cards.
Slot numbers are the address: every coloured thing carries its slot number, and keys 1-9 pick a filament.
Short stencil codes name zones (PLATE, SLOT 02, BIN A3) instead of explanatory hint paragraphs.
Disabled and out-of-bounds states wear a support-pattern hatch rather than fading out.

options.label: Spool Label
options.lineage: filament spool labels and the AMS unit's four numbered windows
options.thesis: Every filament, part and setting is printed like a spool label: colour chip, code, spec table.
options.viewport: Four-slot AMS strip across the top as the filament list, the model below, settings as spec-table label cards.
options.risk: Familiar: close to Bambu Lab's own packaging and app, so it can feel like vendor branding.

options.label: Wiring Schematic
options.lineage: Man-Machine era band identity: neon line diagrams on a strict grid
options.thesis: Colours route to AMS slots along lit lines, like PTFE tubes, drawn on a strict grid.
options.viewport: Colour clusters on the left wired to numbered slots on the right; the model sits where the wires meet.
options.case: Holds product clarity for colour-to-slot mapping; loses on audience identification outside that one step.
options.risk: Reads as a band tribute when the wiring isn't doing real work.

options.label: ASCII Scene
options.lineage: live scenes rendered as typewriter glyphs
options.thesis: The model rendered as glyph density on a strict monospace grid.
options.viewport: The 3D model as a live character grid.
options.case: Hides the colours the product exists to show.
options.kept: One strict rhythm governing the whole composition.

options.label: Teletext
options.thesis: Pages addressed by number on a 40×24 grid.
options.case: Novelty over a tool people use for hours.
options.kept: Direct numeric addressing: slot numbers as keys.

options.label: Starship Terminal
options.thesis: Phosphor readouts and stencilled equipment codes.
options.case: Green phosphor fights the filament colours.
options.kept: Stencil codes that name each zone.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Sections cut and stacked like blocks.
options.case: No tie to printers or drawers.
options.kept: Stacking sections with visible gaps, like layers.

options.label: Stockroom Quotes
options.lineage: industrial streetwear: quoted caps, hazard stripes, zip-tie tags
options.thesis: Literal quoted labels and hazard diagonals.
options.viewport: Quoted zone names over white and black.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean maker-site tool like MakerWorld or Printables, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Top nav, settings sidebar, large 3D canvas, green primary button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
